intro: Shapes, materials and states of matter, the four operations and the first words about space.
p.círculo.consejo: It has an accent on the «í»: THIR-ku-lo. The adjective is «circular» or «redondo».
p.triángulo.consejo: It comes from «tres» and «ángulo». The adjective is «triangular».
p.cuadrado.consejo: It is also an adjective: «una mesa cuadrada». Its four sides measure the same.
p.multiplicar.consejo: It is read «por»: «tres por dos son seis». People do not say «multiplicado por» when speaking.
p.dividir.consejo: In maths it is read «entre»: «seis entre dos son tres».
p.sólido.consejo: It has an accent on the «ó»: SO-li-do. Ice is water in a solid state.
p.líquido.consejo: It has an accent on the «í»: LI-ki-do. A liquid takes the shape of its container.
p.gas.consejo: It is masculine: «el gas». The adjective is «gaseoso».
p.evaporarse.consejo: It is reflexive: «el agua se evapora». It comes from «vapor».
p.congelarse.consejo: It is reflexive: «el agua se congela». Food also freezes in the freezer.
p.hierro.consejo: The h is silent: YE-rro. With «de» you say the material: «una puerta de hierro».
p.método.consejo: It has an accent on the «é»: ME-to-do. A study method is a way of learning.
p.atmósfera.consejo: It has an accent on the «ó»: at-MOS-fe-ra. It is also said of the mood of a place.
p.satélite.consejo: The Moon is a natural satellite of the Earth. There are artificial ones too.
b1.texto:
Today we talk about shapes, science and space.

- **Shapes:** a **círculo** (round), a **triángulo** (triangular), a **cuadrado** (square), a rectangle (rectangular).
- **The four operations:** sumar, restar, **multiplicar** and **dividir**. They are read like this: tres **más** dos son cinco · cinco **menos** dos son tres · tres **por** dos son seis · seis **entre** dos son tres.
- **States of matter:** **sólido**, **líquido** and **gas**. Water **se congela** (freezes) and **se evapora** (evaporates).
- **Materials:** **hierro** (iron), gold, glass, wood. The material is said with **de**: una puerta **de hierro**.
- **Science:** physics, chemistry, a **método**, an experiment.
- **Space:** the **atmósfera** surrounds the Earth; an astronaut travels in a rocket; a **satélite** orbits a planet.
b2.f0.texto: Ice is water in a solid state.
b2.f4.texto: Sea water evaporates with the heat of the sun.
b2.f5.texto: So the water becomes a gas.
b2.f6.texto: How much is six divided by two?
b2.f7.texto: Six divided by two is three.
b2.f8.texto: You have used the right method.
b4.texto:
To talk about natural processes, Spanish uses **se** with the third person of the verb. Nobody does the action: it just happens.

- El agua **se congela** a cero grados.
- El hielo **se derrite** con el calor.
- El agua del mar **se evapora**.

If there are several things, the verb is plural: **se congelan** los lagos; **se evaporan** los charcos.

Compare: **yo congelo** la comida (I do the action); la comida **se congela** (it happens to it).
b4.e1.texto: The puddles evaporate in the sun.
b4.e2.texto: I freeze the soup in the freezer.
b5.f0.texto: Under the summer sun, the ocean water evaporates in silence.
b5.f1.texto: It rises like an invisible thread up to the atmosphere.
b5.f2.texto: There the cold turns it into tiny drops.
b5.f3.texto: The drops form white clouds that cross the sky slowly.
b5.f4.texto: When they reach the mountains, the rain falls on the valleys.
b5.f5.texto: At the poles, the cold turns water into ice as hard as iron.
b5.f6.texto: There the water stays solid for centuries.
b5.f7.texto: A satellite shines over the southern hemisphere like a small star.
b5.f8.texto: From the window of a rocket, an astronaut looks at the blue Earth.
b5.f9.texto: Thanks to that method, scientists know how much ice is left.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! At zero degrees water turns to ice.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Evaporating happens with heat, not with cold.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Dividir» is to split into parts or to do a division of numbers.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Entre» is used to divide: seis entre dos son tres.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Más» is for adding: tres más dos son cinco.
b7.pregunta: Which word is used to multiply?
b8.frase: El agua del mar se evapora con el calor
b8.traduccion: Sea water evaporates with the heat
b9.o0.refuerzo: A square has four sides; a coin has no sides.
b9.o1.refuerzo: A triangle has three sides and three angles.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! A coin is round: a circle.
b11.o0.refuerzo: That's it! There are several lakes: the verb is plural.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Se congela» is singular. With «los lagos» you need the plural.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Without «se», someone freezes the lakes. Here it just happens.
b11.pregunta: Which form goes with a plural subject?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Clouds are in the atmosphere; a satellite orbits outside it.
b12.o1: un objeto que da vueltas a un planeta
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes! The Moon is a natural satellite of the Earth.
b12.o2.refuerzo: A hard metal is iron. A satellite is in space.
p.congela.consejo: From «congelar»: the g sounds like h before e.
p.evapora.consejo: From «evaporar»: the liquid turns into vapour.
p.usado.consejo: Past participle of «usar»: «usado» means already used.
p.evaporan.consejo: From «evaporar»: the plural form of the verb.
p.invisible.consejo: «Invisible» means you cannot see it; it is the same in both sexes.
p.convierte.consejo: From «convertir»: the e takes the diphthong ie.
p.valles.consejo: «Valle» is a valley; the v sounds like b.
p.polos.consejo: «Polo» is a pole of the Earth; the plural is «polos».
p.sólida.consejo: «Sólida» is the feminine form of «sólido»; the accent is on the ó.
p.siglos.consejo: «Siglo» is a century; the plural is «siglos».
p.hemisferio.consejo: «Hemisferio» is half of the Earth; «hemisferio sur» is the southern half.
p.cohete.consejo: «Cohete» is a rocket; the h is silent.
p.astronauta.consejo: «Astronauta» is a person who travels in space.
p.científicos.consejo: «Científico» is a scientist; the c before i sounds like th in Spain.
p.lagos.consejo: «Lago» is a lake; the plural is «lagos».
p.objeto.consejo: «Objeto» can mean a thing; in space it is a body orbiting a planet.
